transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Quantum Health, CTO), Alex Rivera (Quantum Health, Head of MLOps), Sam Cho (Quantum Health, Security Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Priya (Redwood): Hi all, excited to show the Console stuff — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns — basically how you can watch and control inference economics.
[00:18] Maya (Quantum Health): Thanks, Jordan. We're most interested in cost visibility for our patient-facing chat bot and embeddings for search — those are the big cost drivers.
[00:27] Alex (Quantum Health): Also curious about routing — we want low latency for chat but need to keep costs reasonable for background jobs.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood): Totally. We'll start with the Usage Analytics page. You'll see top-level token consumption by route, token-level latency percentiles, and per-model unit cost. Note the per-route cost attribution is tied to route tags you set in the API call.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood): (screen walkthrough) Here is the routes table — chat-customer, embeddings-index, rerank-orders — you can filter by model, by timeframe. It aggregates calls, tokens, median p50/p90 latencies. There's also a breakdown of 'inference cost' vs 'infrastructure overhead' — infrastructure includes reserved Dedicated GPU amortization if you're on Dedicated.
[01:15] Alex (Quantum Health): When you say 'inference cost' is that per-token model cost only or does it include batching efficiency?
[01:21] Priya (Redwood): Good question. The console reports a blended unit cost per token that factors in observed batching efficiency and cache hits during the selected window. It's an empirical number: model runtime cost + observed effective batching / KV cache hit rate adjustments. So if you get a lot of prefix caching those tokens show up as lower effective cost.
[01:40] Sam (Quantum Health): Is KV cache the same as K-V cache? Our docs sometimes say K-V cash, which is a typo.
[01:46] Priya (Redwood): (laughs) Yeah, K-V cache. The transcription sometimes reads it as 'K-V cash' in earlier exports.
[01:52] Jordan (Redwood): One subtlety — Dedicated reserved capacity amortization shows up as a separate line in the cost view so you can see what you're paying for committed GPUs vs per-token runtime.
[02:05] Priya (Redwood): Next, per-route dashboards. You can click a route and get a time series of tokens, latency p50/p90/p99, cost per token, error rate, and tail SLO breaches. We also show a model mix: which model variants served that route over time.
[02:26] Priya (Redwood): (shows example) For chat-customer we show a canary rollout — model-v1 at 80% vs model-v2 quant at 20% — and you can compare quality regressions side-by-side using your eval prompts.
[02:40] Maya (Quantum Health): How do you handle routing when Dedicated capacity runs out or we need to fall back? We need predictable behavior for SLAs.
[02:47] Priya (Redwood): We have smart routing policies. You can configure priority by latency tier (SLO-critical vs background), cost tier, and region. On capacity constraints, policy can fallback to hosted pool or to cheaper quantized variant if you allow that. You can also set guaranteed throughput slices for specific routes.
[03:05] Alex (Quantum Health): For our chat route we need p99 below 300ms for 95% of requests. Can you show latency distribution and how you enforce that?
[03:12] Priya (Redwood): Yes — the dashboard shows tail latency and the Console has alerting on SLO breaches. On the routing side you can pin a route to Dedicated nodes with an autoscale policy, or set a higher cost bucket to favor lower-latency hardware.
[03:27] Jordan (Redwood): Important to note tradeoffs — lower latency often means higher per-token $ because you use more dedicated capacity and smaller batch windows. The Console surfaces the delta so you can make an informed choice.
[03:40] Sam (Quantum Health): Security — how is data handled in Hosted vs Private? We need SOC2 and encryption with KMS, ideally HSM for keys.
[03:48] Jordan (Redwood): For sensitive workloads we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated with VPC peering. All deployments support customer-managed KMS keys; HSM options are available via our enterprise package. We produce audit logs, access traces, and per-request redaction controls.
[04:05] Priya (Redwood): There was a question earlier about SSO and RBAC — Console supports SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC so you can lock routes to specific teams.
[04:16] Maya (Quantum Health): Good. We'll need SOC2 docs and the security questionnaire. Sam will follow up.
[04:22] Sam (Quantum Health): I'll send our questionnaire. Also, show me where the audit logs live in the dashboard.
[04:27] Priya (Redwood): (navigates) Audit logs are accessible under Admin -> Audit. You can export logs to your SIEM or to S3. Each inference request can be traced with a request id, model variant, and route tag.
[04:40] Alex (Quantum Health): On cost breakdown for embeddings — our bulk indexing runs overnight, high throughput but latency-insensitive. Can we route that to cheaper instances?
[04:49] Priya (Redwood): Yes — create a background route tag and set routing policy to cost-first; we'll batch aggressively and you can apply a quantization profile. The Optimize module suggests quant/packing profiles based on your workload to reduce unit cost while preserving quality.
[05:05] Jordan (Redwood): Priya, show the Optimize recommendation we ran for a customer with similar workload.
[05:09] Priya (Redwood): (share) The Optimize page recommends model-quant pairs and autoscaling windows. It also simulates cost impact — e.g., switching to 4-bit quant for embeddings gave a 3x token-cost reduction at 2% similarity delta in quality in their eval set.
[05:28] Maya (Quantum Health): Interesting. How do you validate quality changes? We have strict acceptance criteria for semantic similarity.
[05:33] Priya (Redwood): We run eval sets against your golden prompts and show distribution of metric changes. You can pin regression thresholds; if a rollout causes more than X% drop, it auto-rolls back.
[05:43] Alex (Quantum Health): About instrumentation — how granular is the token breakdown? We need token-level cost within multi-turn chats.
[05:50] Priya (Redwood): We attribute cost to tokens by prefix vs suffix using the KV cache heuristics. Multi-turn chats show effective tokens charged and how many tokens were served from cache vs recomputed. There are cases transcription may mark names wrong, but the console data itself is precise.
[06:08] Sam (Quantum Health): Any compliance caveat for US-EU data residency?
[06:12] Jordan (Redwood): We support regional routing and data residency options for Private deployments. For hosted we have region controls and can ensure data stays in EU or US regions depending on contract.
[06:23] Priya (Redwood): Quick demo of a cost drilldown: click a route -> Cost Analysis -> Model Usage. You can break out cost by model variant, Dedicated amortization, caching savings, and storage/IO overhead. There's also an export CSV for finance.
[06:38] Priya (Redwood): (shows CSV) Example: chat-customer monthly tokens = 120M, effective cost/token = $0.0009, Dedicated amortization = $0.00015/token, net unit cost = $0.00105.
[06:53] Alex (Quantum Health): For forecasting, can we project spend if we scale chat by 2x with different routing decisions?
[06:59] Priya (Redwood): Yes — there's a projection tool where you input growth scenarios and routing mixes; it simulates cost and latency outcomes. You can toggle Dedicated commit levels to see amortization impact.
[07:12] Jordan (Redwood): On the sales side: pilot options — we recommend a 4–6 week pilot focusing on two routes: chat-customer (latency SLO) and embeddings-index (cost-first). We'll run a baseline for one week, then apply Optimize suggestions and measure.
[07:27] Maya (Quantum Health): Sounds good. Timeline-wise we're targeting a Q4 pilot starting mid-Oct.
[07:33] Jordan (Redwood): Great — we'll need access to a dev API key and a small sample of your production traffic for the eval.
[07:40] Alex (Quantum Health): We can provide anonymized traffic with PII redaction.
[07:44] Sam (Quantum Health): Also, we need a draft contract that includes SOC2 appendix and KMS terms.
[07:50] Jordan (Redwood): I'll loop in our legal and security docs. I'll also send the Dedicated pricing grid and a Hosted usage estimate for your expected volumes.
[07:58] Priya (Redwood): Last bit — Alerts and runbooks. Console can trigger pager alerts when SLOs breach and includes runbook templates to triage latency regressions.
[08:08] Maya (Quantum Health): Perfect.
[08:11] Jordan (Redwood): Quick recap and next steps: Jordan to send pricing and contract appendix; Priya to share benchmark sheet, dashboard template, and Optimize guide; Sam to send security questionnaire; Quantum to confirm pilot scope and sample data access.
[08:26] Alex (Quantum Health): Confirmed. We're good to proceed.
[08:30] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks all — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts present (occasional misheard words like 'K-V cash' or 'quantize' as 'con tides') which we've left to preserve realism.
